text: The Two Oceans Marathon is an annual event in Cape Town, South Africa, featuring a 56 kilometres (35 mi) ultramarathon held on a Saturday in April and a 21 kilometres (13 mi) half-marathon on the following Sunday. It was previously held on Easter weekend. Described as "the world's most beautiful marathon," the race takes place against a stunning backdrop of the Cape Peninsula's scenery. Both events begin in Newlands. The ultramarathon follows a largely circular route through Muizenberg, Fish Hoek, over Chapman's Peak, through Hout Bay and Constantia Nek, and concludes at the University of Cape Town campus. When Chapman's Peak Drive is closed due to construction or rock falls, the ultramarathon uses an alternative route via Ou Kaapse Weg. The half-marathon runs along Edinburgh Drive (the M3 highway), then transitions into forest roads past Kirstenbosch, finishing at the University of Cape Town campus. Since its first edition in 1970, the event has expanded, with the half-marathon attracting approximately 16,000 participants—making it the largest half-marathon in South Africa—and the ultramarathon drawing around 11,000 athletes. In addition to the main races, other events are held. The 2020 and 2021 editions were cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Key: Current course record, Course record.
